messages:
Liam: Heads-up — ACME reported that the rerank endpoint is returning a model error and weird score ranges suddenly. They say queries that used to get 0.45-0.9 now return values like -120 to 120 and sometimes an HTTP 410 with body 'model_deprecated'. customer-facing ticket: #2347.
Anya: Can you paste their exact request payload and the error they saw? any request_id or response headers?
Liam: Pasted below (redacted keys). They hit /v1/rerank with model: \"redwood/reranker-alpha\".

Liam: ```json
{
  "model": "redwood/reranker-alpha",
  "query": "best way to compress images for web",
  "candidates": ["Use mozjpeg", "Resize first then compress", "Serve WebP", "Use gzip on static assets"],
  "top_k": 4
}
```

Liam: Response they got:

Liam: ```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "model_deprecated",
    "message": "Model id redwood/reranker-alpha is deprecated. Use redwood/rerank-v2 or redwood/rerank-compat for a compatibility shim.",
    "code": 410
  },
  "request_id": "req_01F8...",
  "server_time_ms": 12
}
```

Anya: thanks. Did they explicitly set any scoring or normalization flags? Any custom scoring function?
Liam: No custom code, they call default API. They called twice: once got 410, once got 200 but the scores were huge negative/positive floats.
Anya: That's consistent with a removed model id sometimes routing to a legacy fallback that returns raw logits instead of normalized relevance scores. Assigning to eng-ml for confirmation. @Marta can you take a look?
Marta: Looking. I pulled the logs for request_id req_01F8... — I can see gateway accepted the old id for a transitional window and routed to the legacy backend 'rerank-legacy' which returns per-candidate logits (un-normalized) while new clients expect [0..1] relevance scores. That mismatch explains the -120..120. Also saw a deprecation banner in the auth header was missed, so clients didn't get the warning.
Marta: Quick repro I ran locally: curl to /v1/rerank with model=redwood/reranker-alpha returns raw logits. Using model=redwood/rerank-v2 returns normalized scores 0.0-1.0.

Marta: Repro commands:

Marta: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood/reranker-alpha","query":"compress images","candidates":["resize","webp","gzip"]}'
```

Marta: Response (legacy):

Marta: ```json
{"scores":[-56.2, 12.3, 8.9], "meta":{"model_id":"rerank-legacy"}}
```

Marta: Response (v2):

Marta: ```json
{"scores":[0.01,0.67,0.32], "meta":{"model_id":"redwood/rerank-v2"}}
```

Raj: Noted. Any production impact beyond the single customer? Can we detect other callers still using the old name?
Marta: We have ~4 customers still hitting the deprecated id in the past 48h. The gateway currently accepts old ids and forwards. I can flip a flag to make the gateway reject deprecated ids immediately, but that will cause 410s instead of noisy logits — but that's safer.

Anya: ACME prefers a quick mitigation so their feature isn't broken. They asked for a short-term mapping so their client keeps working while they update to v2. Is that possible?
Marta: Yes — we can enable a compatibility shim that normalizes logits server-side for 'redwood/reranker-alpha' and also add a Deprecation header in responses. It should be low-risk. I'll prepare a patch to do two things: convert logits -> softmax normalized scores and inject header X-Model-Deprecation: true; recommended-model: redwood/rerank-v2.

Marta: Proposed impl (pseudo):

Marta: ```python
# after routing to legacy backend
logits = resp['scores']  # list of floats
exp = [math.exp(x) for x in logits]
total = sum(exp)
normalized = [e/total for e in exp]
return { 'scores': normalized, 'meta': {'model_id':'redwood/rerank-compat'} }
```

Liam: That sounds good. SLA-wise, this won't affect latency measurably?
Raj: Normalization cost is negligible relative to request overhead. But we should run it in the gateway's fast-path C code or a tiny worker to avoid extra allocations. We'll do a quick perf bench after rollout.

Marta: I pushed a compatibility shim branch and a gateway flag. Deploying to staging now. @deploy-bot, kick a staging rollout for rerank-compat?

deploy-bot: staging rollout started for rerank-compat at 2024-07-03T15:40:00Z (ver: compat-20240703).

Marta: Staging checks green. I validated with the curl repro and normalized scores returned plus header:

Marta: ```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Model-Deprecation: recommended=redwood/rerank-v2; grace_window=30d
Content-Type: application/json

{"scores":[0.02,0.75,0.23],"meta":{"model_id":"redwood/rerank-compat"}}
```

Marta: Rolling to prod in 10m. Will monitor for error spikes.

Anya: I'll message ACME and tell them two things: 1) we enabled a temporary compatibility shim that normalizes scores and 2) they should migrate to redwood/rerank-v2 — include example curl and a migration checklist.

Liam: ACME response: thanks, they can ship the client change tomorrow. They asked whether any billing or quota changes will occur.

Raj: No billing change — rerank units are the same. Also adding a metric to track requests served by the compat shim so we can email customers still on old ids.

Marta: Prod rollout done. Patch id compat-20240703-prod. I also added header with grace_window=30d. We'll auto-return 410 after 30 days unless the customer asks for an extension.

Anya: Sending update to ACME now with the migration snippet and timeline.

Anya: Migration checklist to include in message:
- switch model field to "redwood/rerank-v2"
- ensure candidates array is an array of strings (no nested objects)
- ensure combined token count for query+candidates < 2048 tokens
- remove any client-side assumption that scores are logits (normalize if you do custom handling)

Anya: Message sent. ACME replied: "confirmed — we'll migrate by EOD tomorrow. appreciate quick turnaround :tada:"

Liam: Closing the support ticket as mitigated with follow-ups. Will keep the shim active and report back usage next week.

Marta: Follow-up action items recorded on our side:
- [ENG-ML] instrument compat-shim metrics & alerts
- [ENG-PLATFORM] emit deprecation header for all deprecated ids
- [SUPPORT] email customers using deprecated ids and offer migration help

Raj: Also add a small e2e regression test to ensure new model ids return normalized scores and deprecated ids are flagged.

Anya: Thanks everyone. Marking thread resolved for support routing. If anything else pops up, reopen. :white_check_mark:
